Clustering 3D shapes with ShapeClust

Raydonal Ospina, Inácio R. A. Nascimento, Getúlio J. A. Amaral

Source: vignettes/shapes-3d.Rmd
shapes-3d.Rmd

Overview

Landmark configurations in two or three dimensions are stored as a real k × m × n array: k landmarks, m = 2 or 3 coordinates, n configurations. The functions below work on such arrays directly. The complex 2D interface described in the getting-started vignette is unchanged.

Simulating 3D shapes

sim_shapes3d() draws two groups of configurations around a cube and a parallelepiped template with Gaussian landmark noise, after a random rotation of each configuration. Here n is the number of configurations per group.

library(ShapeClust)

sim <- sim_shapes3d(n = 20, sigma = 0.5, seed = 1)
dim(sim$X)
#> [1]  8  3 40
table(sim$group)
#> 
#>  1  2 
#> 20 20

Distances

shape_distance() returns the Riemannian ("rho"), full Procrustes ("dF") or partial Procrustes ("dP") distance matrix. Reflections are kept as distinct shapes unless reflection = TRUE.

D <- shape_distance(sim$X, "rho")
dim(D)
#> [1] 40 40
round(range(D[upper.tri(D)]), 3)
#> [1] 0.044 1.107

Clustering

shape_kmeans() runs Lloyd’s algorithm with a Procrustes mean shape. shape_pam() and shape_rankkmed() accept the array as well (they compute shape_distance() internally) or a distance matrix.

set.seed(1)
fit_km  <- shape_kmeans(sim$X, K = 2)
fit_pam <- shape_pam(sim$X, K = 2)

table(group = sim$group, kmeans = fit_km$cluster)
#>      kmeans
#> group  1  2
#>     1 20  0
#>     2  0 20
table(group = sim$group, pam = fit_pam$cluster)
#>      pam
#> group  1  2
#>     1 20  0
#>     2  0 20
cat("FMI, k-means:", round(fmi_index(sim$group, fit_km$cluster), 3), "\n")
#> FMI, k-means: 1
cat("FMI, PAM    :", round(fmi_index(sim$group, fit_pam$cluster), 3), "\n")
#> FMI, PAM    : 1

Bagging

bagclust1() takes the same array. With base = "kmeans", each bootstrap replicate fits the centers on the resample and labels all n configurations by the nearest center; the medoid-based bases ("pam", "rankkmed", "clarans", "hill") work on the distance matrix.

fit_bag <- bagclust1(sim$X, K = 2, base = "pam", B = 30, seed = 1)
table(group = sim$group, bagged = fit_bag$cluster)
#>      bagged
#> group  1  2
#>     1 20  0
#>     2  0 20
cat("FMI, bagged PAM:", round(fmi_index(sim$group, fit_bag$cluster), 3), "\n")
#> FMI, bagged PAM: 1

fit_bagk <- bagclust1(sim$X, K = 2, base = "kmeans", B = 10, seed = 1)
cat("FMI, bagged k-means:",
    round(fmi_index(sim$group, fit_bagk$cluster), 3), "\n")
#> FMI, bagged k-means: 1

Clustering tendency

hopkins_shape() tests whether a sample has cluster structure, with a Monte Carlo p-value under a tangent-space Gaussian null.

hopkins_shape(sim$X, B = 49, seed = 1)
#> Hopkins test of clustering tendency (tangent null)
#> H = 0.7347, p = 0.02  (m = 4, power = 1, B = 49)

A real data example: macaque skulls

The macaques data of the shapes package are 7 landmarks in 3D on 18 skulls, nine female and nine male.

data(macaques, package = "shapes")
X <- macaques$x
sex <- macaques$group
dim(X)
#> [1]  7  3 18
table(sex)
#> sex
#> f m 
#> 9 9

set.seed(1)
fit_pam <- shape_pam(X, K = 2)
fit_bag <- bagclust1(X, K = 2, base = "pam", B = 50, seed = 1)

table(sex = sex, pam = fit_pam$cluster)
#>    pam
#> sex 1 2
#>   f 1 8
#>   m 6 3
table(sex = sex, bagged = fit_bag$cluster)
#>    bagged
#> sex 1 2
#>   f 1 8
#>   m 6 3
cat("FMI, PAM       :", round(fmi_index(as.integer(sex), fit_pam$cluster), 3), "\n")
#> FMI, PAM       : 0.622
cat("FMI, bagged PAM:", round(fmi_index(as.integer(sex), fit_bag$cluster), 3), "\n")
#> FMI, bagged PAM: 0.622

Consensus clustering with a representative shape

shape_ensemble() clusters in the leading principal components of the tangent coordinates (enough components for 90% of the variance, between 2 and 10). It runs k-means on bootstrap samples, builds the co-association matrix of the replicates and cuts it with a spectral partition. Each cluster also gets a representative, the observed shape closest to the cluster’s Procrustes mean.

fit_ens <- shape_ensemble(sim$X, K = 2, B = 30, seed = 1)
fit_ens
#> Shape ensemble (tangent PCA, co-association, spectral)
#>   n = 40  K = 2  B = 30  PCA dimension = 2 
#>   cluster sizes: 20 20 
#>   representatives: 15 35
table(truth = sim$group, ensemble = fit_ens$cluster)
#>      ensemble
#> truth  1  2
#>     1 20  0
#>     2  0 20
